items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: He played the piano and I played the piano. We'd pick out some numbers that everybody wanted to use... I've been on a tune too, I have a third of them. Three of us. Jimmy Dupree, Ray McNamara.

ctx.x: I'm making around nearly two hundred after you had extras. If there was any extra money I got it. If one of the places they blew his blues, he said, let Johnny play a chorus, it'll help my organ solo. You know what I mean? The organ used to go up. You know how to do it. And I'd come out of the alcove and put the derby and go in the St. Louis booth. I used to get all the extras. We used to do a radio program for a half hour. I used to get that. Ray McNamara, just Ray McNamara. He played the piano and I played the…
Did Ray McNamara ever write any tunes?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: And every week I had a program with Ray McNamara who incidentally was a very fine organist.

ctx.x: I was curious to know if you felt that, actually, you did go around the country and other places. Yes. Did you feel that you were really ahead of the trends coming from New Orleans, that they discovered a lot of things just a lot later and picked them up, things that had been done a long time before here, like when you were a kid or just coming up in music. And that it just took the rest of the country a long time to discover what was going on here. I think that New Orleans music had an

impression on it, because we used to play on radio, you know. I did a program every Sunday on WWL, and I got plenty of fan mail. When was this? Do you remember? Approximately. That was after Suburban Gardens, and the public's house closed in the early 40s. It was in the 40s. I see. Because I worked steady all the time. And one night I came out of the jazz club. I went on the board of the jazz club. I would talk about it because Miss Moe told me that when I counted the ballots, I didn't have one dissenting vote,…
But how many members were in your band in the twenties?
